text: Provide a native profiler: sampling CPU and GPU profiles attributed to Task and Component rather than threads, flame graphs by TaskGroup, exportable with traces.
Decide that Rust std support for native targets lives at Layer 3 as a compatibility crate over the native SDK; no Layer 1 entry point may be justified by std's POSIX-shaped APIs.
Decide the license of the native SDK, runtime and language bindings and state explicitly that proprietary native applications are permitted.
rationale: Gaming and commercial software are product objectives, and developers will not target a platform whose SDK terms are unclear.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Create and maintain a dedicated Rust target triple for native userspace (e.g. x86_64-unknown-jakeos) with a std/alloc port over the native ABI, initially as a custom JSON target and later proposed for tier-3 upstream inclusion.
rationale: Native applications must not be compiled as Linux binaries or the native ABI firewall in §3 is silently violated by the toolchain itself.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Build an SDK-level compatibility suite that compiles applications against SDK version N and runs them on system generation N+1 (and vice versa where promised) to enforce the Layer 2 versioning rules of §66.
rationale: Interface versioning is only real if something tests old binaries against new platforms on every merge.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Distribute versioned developer toolchains (rustc target, IDL compiler, image tools, QEMU harness) as immutable packages installable on Linux and macOS hosts and natively on JakeOS with a single toolchain manager command.
rationale: Third-party developers in V3 cannot be expected to reproduce the project's build environment by hand.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Provide a single developer command that builds, boots the result in QEMU and runs the same test harness CI uses, with a target of under 30 minutes from fresh clone to a booted QEMU image on a standard Linux host.
rationale: Contributor onboarding time is the primary constraint on the community §56.5 says the project cannot succeed without.

lens: Boot, firmware, platform security and identity
text: Make the native runtime enable userspace exploit mitigations by default (ASLR, NX, CET shadow stacks and IBT where the CPU supports them, guard pages, hardened allocator) and expose them as component manifest requirements.
rationale: §51 lists language and capability safety but omits the conventional process-level mitigations that still matter for C and unsafe Rust code.

text: ADR on the interactive command shell: a POSIX shell inside the Linux personality versus a native object-aware shell that speaks typed interfaces, and how the os CLI, PTYs, and job control map onto tasks and channels.
rationale: Developers live in the terminal from V1 and the shell defines whether the native object model is reachable from the command line.

text: Ship a hardware probe tool that produces an anonymized device fingerprint and test results that can populate the compatibility database.
rationale: A compatibility database with no ingestion path stays empty.

text: Ship a built-in bug reporter that bundles generation ID, hardware fingerprint, relevant traces and inspect output with user-controlled redaction.
rationale: Good bug reports require data users cannot be expected to gather by hand.

text: Provide an os bisect tool that steps between generations to locate the generation that introduced a regression.
rationale: Immutable generations make regression bisection cheap and it turns vague reports into actionable ones.

text: Provide a cross-compilation SDK and emulator/VM harness so native applications can be built and tested from Linux, macOS and Windows hosts and in hosted CI without running JakeOS.
rationale: Developers will not adopt a platform they must install to compile for; the first native apps will be built from other OSes.

text: Set an onboarding target: a new developer goes from SDK download to a running hello-component in under 15 minutes on any major host OS, measured by timed onboarding sessions each release.
rationale: Time-to-first-component is the strongest predictor of whether a developer continues.

text: Publish a porting guide mapping POSIX and Win32 concepts to native primitives (file descriptors to capabilities, fork to Components, signals to cancellation, sockets to channels) with worked ports of real applications.
rationale: Every developer arriving has a Unix or Windows mental model and the native model is only adoptable if the translation is written down.

text: Provide LSP-based tooling, a Debug Adapter Protocol debugger for components, and remote-development integration (VS Code, JetBrains) into a JakeOS VM or device.
rationale: Developers keep their editors; the OS must meet them there rather than require a new IDE.

text: Provide an os publish CLI and hosted CI integrations (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI) that build, sign and submit packages.
rationale: Developers publish from CI, not from a desktop; friction here directly limits catalogue growth.

text: Native applications must see none of the Linux or Windows constructs unless explicitly using a compatibility environment.
Native applications execute against the Native Platform layer (SDK + platform services) rather than the kernel directly.
Worked PhotoEditor capability example must ship as an SDK sample and as an integration test proving the denied capabilities are absent.
Isolation must be cheap enough that 'isolate it' is the default; SDK defaults create separate components without asking.
Support a browser-shaped graph: a UI component, a Network component, per-Tab Renderer and JavaScript Runtime components, and a Download Manager component.
ImageDecoder reference component: Input<ImageBytes>, Output<Bitmap>, memory budget 256 MB, CPU budget 25%.
Maximum-performance native software must remain free to compile directly to machine code.
Ship the ImageDecoder interface and service as the reference typed service used by the V0 demo.
Memory movement must prefer capability/ownership transfer over copying; SDK APIs default to move semantics for MemoryObjects.
The tiny native runtime (cross-ref §59) must provide an async executor that drives futures from Operation completions without wrapping blocking Linux syscalls.
The SDK must expose operation.cancel() as the cancellation entry point for an outstanding Operation.
The SDK must expose operation.deadline(...) to attach or modify a deadline on an outstanding Operation.
The SDK must expose operation.await so an Operation integrates with Rust async/await and suspends the owning Task until completion.
The runtime must support an async fn programming model in which awaiting a database.get() or request.respond() style operation suspends only the Task, not the execution context.
Provide a trace viewer or exporter usable from os trace (cross-ref §64) to inspect Component, Task, Channel, and Operation timelines.
The SDK must expose files.choose<T>() returning a typed UserSelected<T> capability after the user selects an object.
Provide package build tooling in the SDK that produces a manifest and content-addressed package from a native project.
Decide the native linking model (static linking, dynamic linking against content-addressed shared objects, or both) and its effect on startup sharing (cross-ref §34).
Implement the system history (os history) command listing events with timestamp and human-readable description.
Implement system restore <point> (os restore) that returns the system to the state recorded at a chosen history event.
Restore must be able to revert application state where applications opt in to state checkpointing.
Client libraries and the SDK must support detecting service disconnect on a Channel.
Client libraries must support rebinding to a restarted service instance by interface name rather than by dead endpoint.
Client libraries must support retry of idempotent Operations after rebind with defined semantics.
Client libraries must support restore-state: re-establishing session state (surfaces, streams, subscriptions) with a restarted service.
Executables and dependencies must be memory-mapped directly from the content store at launch.
Launch metadata (component graph, capability set, relocation state) must be cached aggressively across launches.
Implement the os env enter command that materialises an environment from environment.yaml and drops the developer into it.
Implement the remaining os env lifecycle subcommands implied by enter (list, exit/leave, status, destroy, rebuild).
Semantic interfaces must support scripting clients (shell/CLI invocation of app interfaces).
Semantic interfaces must support testing clients; build a UI test harness that drives applications through their semantic interfaces.
Provide a Rust user-space SDK binding (primary).
Provide a C SDK binding.
Provide a C++ SDK binding.
Provide a Swift SDK binding.
Provide a Kotlin SDK binding.
Provide a C# SDK binding.
Provide a TypeScript/Wasm SDK binding via the Wasm component integration (§13).
Decide the order and milestone of SDK language bindings (Rust V0, C V1, C++ V2, others V3+) (ADR).
Unsafe native code must remain possible for applications and drivers that need it.
The SDK must make the secure and fast path the easiest path for developers.
Implement the #[component] entry-point attribute macro generating component bootstrap, runtime and tracing setup.
Implement the Context (ctx) object that exposes exactly the capabilities granted to the component.
Implement ctx.ui.window() returning a native window object (§60).
Implement ctx.files.choose::<Image>() invoking the OS chooser and returning a typed capability (§25).
Provide an image decoding library or decoder service (decode(image) -> Bitmap) in the SDK running as an isolated component (§11 ImageDecoder).
Implement window.render(bitmap) presenting a Buffer to a Surface via the native UI protocol.
SDK-written code must naturally result in explicit capabilities (no ambient access APIs in the SDK).
SDK-written code must naturally result in structured task ownership (all spawned tasks belong to a TaskGroup, §21).
SDK-written code must naturally result in async I/O (no blocking I/O primitives in the default SDK surface, §18).
SDK-written code must naturally result in typed IPC (generated stubs only, §14).
SDK-written code must naturally result in safe object lifetimes (capabilities released on drop, no dangling handles).
SDK-written code must naturally result in automatic tracing of components, tasks and operations (§24).
SDK-written code must naturally result in appropriate cancellation propagation (§21).
Developers must not have to fight the OS to do the right thing; every SDK ergonomics regression is a bug.
Implement the tiny native async runtime (§59) that multiplexes Tasks over kernel Operations and completions.
Provide a project scaffolding tool (e.g. os new) generating a component with manifest, requested capabilities and build config.
Define the SDK versioning and compatibility policy as stability layer 3 (§66): evolves quickly, semver, deprecation windows (ADR).
Define the SDK Result/error model mapping kernel failure semantics (cancelled, revoked, disconnected, deadline exceeded) to typed errors.
Provide a component testing harness with mock capabilities and mock services.
Integrate debugger support (breakpoints, async task inspection) with the SDK runtime (§61).
Integrate the SDK build (cargo) with the package format so a build emits an immutable Package with manifest (§28).
Native application startup must not perform dynamic shared-library loading via a path-based loader (ld.so-style).
Native application startup should avoid executing global constructors/initialisers on the critical path where the SDK can precompute state.
A published SDK (cross-ref §52).
Study Rust async (Future, Pin, Waker) for zero-cost mapping of kernel Operations onto SDK futures.
Study Tokio runtime (work stealing, task budgets, cooperative scheduling) for the native runtime executor design.
A tiny native runtime (async executor, channel bindings, capability handle wrappers) sufficient to write the V0 demo in Rust.
Stable native SDK with a documented versioning and deprecation policy.
Debugging: debugger attach to native components, symbolisation, crash dumps.
Developer tooling is built from the beginning: 'os inspect' and 'os trace' ship in V0, not after the platform stabilises.
'os inspect component' command.
'os inspect task' command.
'os inspect channel' command.
'os inspect capability' command.
'os inspect memory' command for MemoryObjects.
'os inspect resource' command for ResourceDomains.
'os trace' command for structured, dynamically enabled tracing.
'os history' command listing system state-change events (cross-ref §31).
'os restore' command restoring to a prior point in system history.
'os env' command family for development environments (cross-ref §35).
'os' CLI provides machine-readable (JSON) output and shell completions for use by scripts and AI agents.
Layer 3 native SDK that evolves relatively quickly under semantic versioning.
Layer 4 frameworks (UI toolkit, app frameworks) that can evolve rapidly independent of lower layers.
